about: Review #471 A1 (lab PR 267): a root process staged in /tmp connects out, then executes /usr/bin/dpkg in the same pid; no credential read. Taken ahead of the connect, the dpkg exec made NET-008 a Log and dropped CHAIN-002; judged as of the connect's time, the flow is the staging exec's.

switches.held: the kill of the shell's process tree (R020, lab PR 224)
the kill of one process past the scan kill threshold (NN-L-NET-026, lab PR 224)
the kill of one process past the brute-force kill threshold (NN-L-NET-027, lab PR 224)
the kill for a flow to port 53 of a server that is no configured resolver (port 53 was exempt before lab PR 224)
the kill of an allowlisted transfer tool whose lineage holds a precursor (exempt before lab PR 224)
the kill of the ransomware actor's process tree (NN-L-IMP-001, lab PR 225)
the kill of the staged program that asked a security tool off (NN-L-EVA, lab PR 225)
the kill for a rename seen only as a watched directory's new entry (NN-L-FIM-010, a match added by lab PR 225)

decision.name: Root exec from user-writable path
decision.reasoning: Root execution from user-writable path — privilege escalation indicator [also matched: R001_ExecFromTmp (KillProcessTree, Medium)]

decision.name: /tmp exec followed by network egress
decision.reasoning: Process executed from a staging directory (/tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm) then opened an outbound flow (other than a lookup at a configured resolver) within the correlation window — dropper C2 (T1059 → T1571); kill the process tree + posture → COMBAT [also matched: NN-L-NET-008_OutboundFromTmpExec (KillProcess, High)] [judged at the connect, while the flow is open (lab PR 224)]
